public_rationale: The research supports the description of scaling laws as empirical relationships. It does not establish that scaling cannot reach AGI. No decisive event meeting the resolution rule was established by the evaluation date. An indefinite negative forecast cannot be credited merely because a qualifying success has not been demonstrated.
limitations: Public model documentation may not disclose enough to establish scaling-only provenance.
The empirical clause and the AGI forecast have different evidentiary requirements.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Pure scaling of LLMs by adding data and compute to existing architectures will not reach AGI; scaling laws are empirical generalizations, not physical laws.

statement.excerpt: A key claim of the paper was that pure scaling of LLMs – just adding more data and compute to extant LLM architectures – would not bring us to AGI, and that so-called scaling laws were merely empirical generalizations rather than physical laws.
statement.document_title: Five ways in which the last 3 months — and especially the DeepSeek era — have vindicated “Deep learning is hitting a wall"

from_speaker: just adding more data and compute to extant LLM architectures
would not bring us to AGI
merely empirical generalizations rather than physical laws
our_interpretation: The forecast concerns increasing training data and compute without additional reasoning methods or other substantive changes.
AGI means broadly general, human-level intellectual capability established through independent evaluation, rather than success on one benchmark.
The empirical status of scaling laws is a separate, presently checkable clause. Establishing it does not establish the forecast.
Pure scaling restricts the proposed route to AGI; it is not a separate contingent antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently general result establishing that the specified scaling-only approach cannot attain AGI would support the forecast. Research describing fitted empirical relationships supports only the scaling-law clause.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A system independently established as AGI, with documentation showing that its qualifying capabilities arose solely from increased data and training compute on the relevant existing LLM architectures.

evidence.explanation: The researchers explicitly describe empirical relationships for language-model loss. This supports that clause but supplies no impossibility result about reaching AGI through scaling.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Independent validation of AGI accompanied by a documented scaling-only development history, or a general impossibility result covering the specified approach.
